message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively—but they share a common ancestor within the clade **Laurasiatheria**. That last common ancestor was a small, insectivorous mammal that lived roughly 90 million years ago, during the late Cretaceous period.
